### Some Mock, Others Believe: Pondering Strangeness in Our Preaching
Author: David Mathis
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/some-mock-others-believe
Passage: Acts 17:20
Points:
- Proclaiming Christ and the resurrection inevitably sounds strange to an unbelieving culture.
- Righteous distress over surrounding idolatry should prompt measured, reasoned engagement rather than angry outbursts.
- Ridicule from skeptics should be ignored so that it does not distract from listeners with honest questions.
- Faithful gospel communicators build common ground without diluting the supernatural core of the message.

### Day 261: Acts 17:15–23
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-261-acts-17-1523.html
Passage: Acts 17:15-23
Points:
- Paul faced the pervasive idolatry of Athens alone while waiting for his companions.
- Rather than shrinking back in intimidation, deep concern for the lost moved him to speak daily.
- He initiated spiritual conversations with anyone who would listen in both religious and secular settings.
- He bridged cultural gaps by using Athenian reference points to introduce the true God.
